page: Amazon Web Services c7i.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz with 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs, accompanied by 105 MB of L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 192.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, delivering a dedicated 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions are extensive, including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 matrix operations, as well as hardware cryptographic primitives such as VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers top-tier parallel compute capability, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 86,485.53 and strong multi-core Geekbench performance of 19,529.0. CPU encryption testing reaches top-decile performance at 89,335.3 points, enabled by specialized hardware instructions. Memory subsystems sustain 209.23 GB/s during large-block read operations. For targeted machine learning inference, the integrated AMX and AVX-512 engines handle 3,413.27 tokens per second on prompt processing for lightweight 135M models and 287.32 tokens per second on 7B models.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on network compute density over integrated disk storage. The instance includes 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides zero local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for persistent data. There are also no discrete GPUs bundled. Single-core stress tests land in the median range with a score of 2,019.6, indicating that the instance's primary computational advantage lies in dense multi-threaded throughput and specialized instruction sets rather than single-threaded clock scaling.

The resource profile offers strong compute efficiency for workloads that can fully exploit its 96 vCPUs and DDR5 subsystem without requiring large local scratch disks. The c7i.24xlarge is well matched for high-throughput batch compilation, video and image processing, static web serving infrastructure, network-bound in-memory caching such as Redis, and CPU-based deep learning inference workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.24xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 48-core, 96-thread Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It pairs 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz with 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, establishing a focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution, with a PassMark CPU score of 86,485.53, top-tier encryption ratings, and solid AMX-accelerated CPU inference speeds. The platform carries no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, prioritizing network-attached resources and raw CPU cycles over localized disk persistence. With dedicated compute execution, fast DDR5 throughput, and broad vector instruction support, the c7i.24xlarge suits large-scale software builds, image processing, CPU-based matrix operations, and high-concurrency microservices.
